title: Search & Indexing
summary: Full-text search isn't a fancy `LIKE` — it's an inverted index for speed plus a relevance model for quality, wrapped in a distributed system behind one search box.

blocks.markdown:
Search flips the problem: instead of scanning rows, build a **word → documents** map once and look it up.

- An **inverted index** maps each term to the list of docs that contain it — like a book's back-index.
- **Analysis** turns text into terms; **ranking** (BM25) puts the best results first.
- **Lucene** is the engine; **Elasticsearch / OpenSearch / Solr** make it distributed with **shards** and **replicas**.
- You pay extra at **write** time so **reads** are fast and rankable.

blocks.subTitle: When to reach for it
blocks.markdown:
Pick the tool to the need — search engines aren't always the answer.

| Need | Reach for |
|---|---|
| Exact key, transactions | Relational DB |
| Full-text + ranking + facets | Elasticsearch / Solr |
| Prefix autocomplete | Trie / FST |
| Tiny dataset, plain contains | `LIKE` or in-memory filter |

blocks.subTitle: The inverted index
blocks.markdown:
An inverted index stores **term → posting list**: the doc IDs containing that term.

![Inverted index mapping terms to posting lists](assets/search-indexing/inverted-index.svg)

- A **posting** holds the doc ID, usually the **term frequency**, and optionally **positions** (for phrase queries).
- Posting lists are **sorted by doc ID** and compressed, so `fast AND car` is a cheap two-pointer **intersection**.
- The **term dictionary** is stored as an **FST** — compact and good for prefix/fuzzy lookups.

assets.alt: Inverted index mapping terms to posting lists

blocks.subTitle: Analysis: text into terms
blocks.markdown:
Text never goes in raw — an **analyzer** pipeline normalizes it first.

- **Character filters** clean raw text (strip HTML, map `&`→"and").
- **Tokenizer** splits on whitespace/punctuation: `"Fast, red cars!"` → `[fast, red, cars]`.
- **Token filters** lowercase, drop **stopwords** ("the", "a"), **stem** to roots (`cars`→`car`), apply **synonyms**.

The #1 search rule: **the same analyzer must run at index and query time**, or tokens never line up and you get zero hits.

blocks.subTitle: Stemming vs lemmatization
blocks.markdown:
Both reduce words to a common form so "running" matches "run".

- **Stemming** is rule-based and fast (Porter), but crude — it can merge "universe" and "university".
- **Lemmatization** is dictionary-based and returns real words, but slower.
- Most systems use **stemming** by default.
- Some fields want **no analysis** at all — `keyword` type for product codes, IDs, exact names.

blocks.subTitle: Ranking with BM25
blocks.markdown:
Matching gives a *set*; ranking gives an *order*. Classic scoring has two halves:

- **TF** — more occurrences of a query term means more relevant.
- **IDF** — rare terms ("carburetor") are discriminating; common ones ("the") aren't. Weight rare terms up.

**BM25** is the default since ~2016. It keeps IDF but fixes TF-IDF with:
- **Saturation** (`k1`≈1.2) — the 20th occurrence barely adds score.
- **Length normalization** (`b`≈0.75) — long docs don't win just by being big.

blocks.subTitle: The query path
blocks.markdown:
A query walks **analyze → match → rank → top-N**.

![Query analyze match rank flow](assets/search-indexing/query-flow.svg)

- The raw string is **analyzed** with the *same* pipeline used at index time into terms.
- Terms are **matched** against posting lists to find candidate docs.
- Each candidate is **ranked** by BM25 and the **top-N** are returned sorted.
- The analyzer on both sides is what makes the tokens line up.

blocks.subTitle: Segments & near-real-time
blocks.markdown:
Lucene writes immutable **segments** — small self-contained inverted indexes.

- New docs buffer in memory, then flush as a new segment; segments are **never modified**.
- **Immutable** means lock-free reads, easy page-cache use, trivial copy-for-replication.
- A delete is just a **tombstone** in a bitmap; space is reclaimed during background **merges**.
- A new doc is searchable only after a **refresh** (~1 s in ES) — **near-real-time**, not instant. A **translog** (WAL) keeps it durable before that.

blocks.subTitle: Shards & replicas
blocks.markdown:
One Lucene index lives on one machine. To scale, an index is split into **shards**.

![Elasticsearch shards and replicas across nodes](assets/search-indexing/shards-replicas.svg)

- Each **shard** is an independent Lucene index; a doc routes via `hash(id) % primaries`.
- **Primary shard count is fixed at creation** — changing the divisor re-buckets every doc.
- **Replicas** are copies on other nodes for **HA** and **read throughput**.
- A query **scatter-gathers**: each shard returns local top-K, the coordinator merges to global top-N. Latency is bound by the **slowest shard**.

assets.alt: Elasticsearch shards and replicas across nodes

blocks.subTitle: Autocomplete with tries
blocks.markdown:
Typeahead is a **prefix** problem, not a term problem — the inverted index is the wrong tool.

- A **trie** (prefix tree) spells a prefix along each root path; lookup is **O(prefix length)**.
- Walking "c→a→r" lands on a subtree whose leaves are all completions of "car".
- Lucene's completion suggester uses an in-memory **FST** for sub-millisecond responses.
- Build a **separate** suggestion index, often weighted so popular completions rank first.

blocks.subTitle: The dials you turn
blocks.markdown:
Every search system trades along a few axes.

| Dial | Toward A | Toward B |
|---|---|---|
| Refresh interval | Fresher (1 s) | Higher throughput (30 s) |
| Matching | High recall (synonyms) | High precision (strict) |
| Shards | More parallelism | Less scatter overhead |
| Replicas | More read HA | Less write cost |

Keep shards roughly **10–50 GB**; avoid thousands of tiny ones.

blocks.subTitle: Real systems
blocks.markdown:
The same Lucene core powers many engines; they differ on distribution.

- **Elasticsearch / OpenSearch** — Lucene + shards, replicas, translog, JSON query DSL.
- **Apache Solr** — Lucene with SolrCloud + ZooKeeper coordination; strong faceting.
- **Google Search** — web-scale inverted index plus **PageRank** (link-graph importance).
- **Postgres FTS** — a real inverted index (GIN over `tsvector`) inside the DB; great when search is a *feature*, not the product.

blocks.subTitle: What to monitor
blocks.markdown:
Search is invisible until the tail latency climbs. Watch:

- **p99 query latency** — rising with steady traffic means hot shards, too many segments, or GC pressure.
- **Indexing queue depth / rejections** — writes outpacing capacity; back off or scale out.
- **Merge time & segment count** — long merges signal too-short a refresh interval.
- **Cluster color** — yellow = missing replicas (degraded); red = missing primary (data loss risk).
- **Zero-result rate / nDCG** — the search-*quality* signal most engineers forget.

The myths that bite in interviews and production:

- **"Search is a fancy `LIKE`."** It's an index for retrieval *plus* a ranking model — the ranking is where the value lives.
- **"Indexed docs are instantly searchable."** Durable fast (translog), searchable only after refresh (~1 s). Index-then-query tests flake.
- **"More shards = faster."** Past a point, scatter-gather overhead and memory dominate.
- **"Stemming always helps."** It can merge unrelated words and break exact-match fields.
- **"BM25 understands meaning."** It's pure term statistics — synonyms and vector search are separate layers.
